label: Keep warnings out of saved notes
title: Stopped a safety warning from being replayed in the next session
summary: I fixed a bug where a one-time safety-stop message was saved as a task and shown again at the start of the next session.
cvLine: Fixed session-summary generation in an AI coding-agent hook so safety-classifier notices are no longer persisted and re-injected into later sessions; added regression tests covering the filtered, notice-only and mid-sentence cases

story.title: Stop old warnings from coming back as tasks
story.lead: ECC saves a short summary at the end of each coding session and shows it at the start of the next one. A safety-stop message was ending up in that summary.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: When a response was stopped by the safety classifier, the notice was saved as if the user had asked for it. The next session then showed it again as a past task, which could trigger the same warning repeatedly.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I made the summary step ignore messages that start with that safety-stop notice, while keeping any normal message that only mentions the phrase in the middle of a sentence.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added three tests for this; the session-end test file passes (21 of 21) and two of the new tests fail without the fix. I could not trigger a real safety stop, so the notice shape comes from the issue report.

label: Keep terminal commands working at startup
diagramTitle: Declare terminal support before the sandbox is ready
footNote: Commands work from the first try
title: Stopped the first command from timing out while a sandbox starts
summary: I fixed a bug where a command sent to a sandbox that was still starting up was treated as a one-off job and timed out, instead of running in a proper terminal.
cvLine: Fixed deferred sandbox startup in an AI security-testing agent so backends declare terminal (PTY) support up front and the first shell command keeps its interactive session; added regression tests, including one on the SDK's real local sandbox client

story.title: Make the first command work while the sandbox is still starting
story.lead: Strix can start its sandbox in the background so the agent does not have to wait. Until it finished starting, it told the tools that terminals were not available.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: While the sandbox was still starting, it reported that it had no terminal support. The agent library checked this straight away, so it left out the tool for typing into a running command and ran the first command as a one-off job. That command then hit a hard time limit and never returned a session to continue with.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: Each sandbox backend now says up front whether it supports terminals, and the built-in Docker one does. The still-starting sandbox repeats that answer until it is ready, then goes back to asking the real sandbox. Backends that do not say anything behave as before.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added three tests, including the bug report's reproduction using the library's real local sandbox. The test file passes with 13 tests. The full suite has the same 19 failures as the main branch, and the code checks (ruff, mypy, bandit) pass.

label: Wait for provider reset before retrying
diagramTitle: Schedule heartbeat retries after limit reset
title: Stopped heartbeat retries from hammering providers after usage limit errors
summary: I fixed a bug where agent heartbeats retried every 30 seconds after hitting a provider usage limit, scheduling a single retry after the reset time instead.
cvLine: Fixed agent heartbeat retry scheduler to extract UTC usage-limit reset times and schedule a single retry at reset plus one minute, preventing provider retry storms; validated with comprehensive unit and database integration tests

story.title: Stop heartbeat retry storms after provider usage limits
story.lead: When an agent run hit a provider usage limit error, the retry scheduler hammered the provider every 30 seconds until attempts were exhausted.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: Ordinary transient retries kept hammering the provider every ~30s after a usage-limit error (e.g. You've hit your limit · resets 3pm), wasting API calls while the quota window remained exhausted.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I added a helper to parse the UTC reset clock from error messages or structured retryNotBefore values, capped limit retries at 1 attempt, and scheduled the retry at reset time plus 1 minute. Ambiguous reset clocks cleanly suppress fast retries.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: Validated with 31 passing unit tests and a database integration test in Vitest, along with passing module boundary and map checks.

title: Stopped successful Prem AI calls being reported as errors
summary: I fixed OpenLIT so that normal Prem AI chat and embedding calls are recorded as successful, with their token counts, instead of as errors with no usage.
cvLine: Fixed OpenTelemetry instrumentation for the Prem AI SDK that exported successful non-streaming chat and embedding calls as ERROR spans without token usage, by normalising SDK response objects before reading them; added hermetic regression tests (21 passing) and verified the before and after behaviour

story.title: Report successful Prem AI calls as successful
story.lead: OpenLIT records traces of AI calls. With Prem AI, normal calls that worked were being recorded as errors and without token counts.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: Recent Prem AI versions return their replies as objects rather than plain dictionaries. OpenLIT read them as dictionaries, hit an error, and so every successful non-streaming chat and embedding call was recorded as an error with no token usage.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I reused the conversion that OpenLIT already applied to streamed replies for the non-streaming chat and embedding calls, so the reply is turned into a dictionary before it is read. An embedding reply without usage data no longer causes an error either.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: In an offline before-and-after check with the real Prem AI 0.3.107 reply types, the calls went from ERROR with no token counts to OK with token counts, finish reason and response id. The new and existing Prem AI tests give 21 passing, and pylint scores 10.00/10.

bannerAlt: Headroom's official repository banner showing context compression and preserved content
label: Show server rejections instead of hiding them
diagramTitle: Stop retrying requests the server rejected
title: Stopped the TypeScript client hiding server rejections behind retries
summary: I fixed Headroom's TypeScript client so that when the server rejects a request as invalid, the app is told right away instead of the client retrying and silently carrying on.
cvLine: Fixed TypeScript SDK error handling so typed 4xx proxy errors are rethrown instead of retried and swallowed by the fallback path, and made the error-type lookup safe against inherited object keys; validated with 7 new regression tests (456 SDK tests passing) and a local HTTP stub reproduction

story.title: Show the real error when the server rejects a request
story.lead: Headroom's TypeScript client talks to a proxy that compresses AI requests. When the proxy rejected a request as invalid, the client could hide that answer.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: When the proxy replied with a specific kind of 4xx rejection, such as a configuration or validation error, the client treated it like a temporary failure. It retried the request and, with the default settings, quietly returned the uncompressed data, so the caller never saw the rejection. The lookup that turns the proxy's error type into an error class could also pick up built-in object names like constructor by mistake.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: The client now stops and reports any specific error that carries a status below 500, while server-side (5xx) and connection errors are still retried as before. The error-type lookup now only accepts names that were deliberately listed.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added 7 regression tests, and 6 of them fail without the fix. The full TypeScript SDK test suite passes (456 passed, 33 skipped), and type checking and the build pass. A before-and-after run against a local stub server shows the rejection now reaching the caller after a single request.

diagramTitle: Track quote depth for every line

footNote: Quoted code and headings are bounded correctly
title: Made plugin checks understand text inside nested quotes
summary: I fixed a bug where a checker for AI plugins misread code and headings inside quoted Markdown, so it could pair up the wrong pieces of text.
cvLine: Fixed Markdown parsing in a plugin-evaluation tool by tracking blockquote nesting depth per line so fenced code, headings and blank lines inside quotes bound code spans as CommonMark specifies; added three regression tests and validated with 770 passing tests

story.title: Make quoted code and headings end where they should
story.lead: The plugin checker finds references to other files in plugin documents, and it skips code. Quoted text, lines starting with >, confused it.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: The checker ignored how deeply a line was quoted. A code block opened inside a nested quote stayed open after the quote ended, a heading inside a quote did not end a paragraph, and a line holding only > was not seen as blank. A stray backtick could then pair with one in the next paragraph.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: It now counts the > markers on each line and applies the code block, heading and list rules to the text after them. A code block closes when a line is quoted less deeply than where it opened, and a line of only > counts as blank. It follows the plan the maintainer wrote in the issue.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added one test for each case in the issue. They fail on the main branch and pass with the fix. The full suite passes with 770 tests, and the lint, validation and version checks are clean. The 9 smoke tests that need other tools installed were skipped.

label: Check image links where the download really goes
diagramTitle: Fetch reference images through the safe downloader
footNote: Proxy settings and IPv6 tricks no longer bypass the check
title: Closed two ways around InvokeAI's safety check for image links
summary: I fixed InvokeAI's image search so that a proxy setting or a special IPv6 address can no longer trick it into fetching from the machine it runs on.
cvLine: Hardened a server-side image URL fetch against SSRF by routing it through the project's guarded HTTP session, which ignores ambient proxy settings and checks the connected peer, and by reusing the shared URL validator so NAT64 addresses are rejected; validated with 3 new regression tests that fail before the fix (172 tests passing across the SSRF and image-map suites)

story.title: Make the image-link safety check match where the bytes really come from
story.lead: InvokeAI's semantic search can fetch a reference image from a link. It checks the link's address first, so it should never reach the server's own network.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: The check looked at the address of the link, but the download then used a plain web request. If a proxy was set in the environment, the request went through the proxy, not to the address that was checked. Separately, the special IPv6 address 64:ff9b::7f00:1 is reported as a public address but maps back to the local machine (127.0.0.1), so it passed the check.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: The download now goes through the project's existing guarded session, which ignores proxy settings and checks the address it actually connects to. The old hand-written address check now uses the shared validator, which blocks these special IPv6 ranges. The per-redirect checks and the error response are unchanged.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added three regression tests: redirects are still re-checked through the guarded session, the special IPv6 address is rejected before any request is made, and proxy settings are ignored. All three fail on the old code and pass now. The SSRF and image-map test files pass together (172 passed), and the lint and format checks pass.

label: Skip redundant negative pass at guidance scale 1
diagramTitle: Run single-batch denoising when guidance scale is 1
flow:

for every step

when scale is 1

and memory use
footNote: Guidance scale 1.0 discards the negative prompt mathematically, so computing it was pure waste
title: Eliminated wasted model passes during Stable Diffusion 3 generation without guidance
summary: I optimized InvokeAI's Stable Diffusion 3 denoising loop so generation at guidance scale 1.0 skips loading negative conditioning and halves model compute by dropping the unconditional pass.
cvLine: Eliminated redundant negative conditioning and unconditional transformer forward passes in Stable Diffusion 3 denoising when guidance scale equals 1.0, halving transformer compute and activation memory for Turbo workflows; verified with 3 regression unit tests (4 passed across the SD3 suite)

story.title: Skip the unconditional pass in SD3 generation when guidance scale is 1.0
story.lead: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large Turbo defaults to a classifier-free guidance scale of 1.0. At scale 1.0, the negative conditioning is mathematically discarded, but InvokeAI was still loading it and computing it every step.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: Classifier-free guidance combines conditional and unconditional passes: output = uncond + scale * (cond - uncond). When scale is exactly 1.0, this formula simplifies to output = cond. Despite this, InvokeAI's SD3 denoising node hardcoded guidance enabled, loaded negative text conditioning, and fed a doubled batch (both negative and positive) through the multi-billion parameter transformer at every step, wasting half the compute and activation memory.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I updated the denoising routine to check whether any step actually uses guidance. When all steps use guidance scale 1.0, loading negative conditioning is skipped entirely and the transformer runs with batch size 1 directly on positive conditioning. For schedules with mixed scales, negative conditioning is loaded once and individual 1.0 steps execute without batching.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added unit tests covering scalar scale 1.0, standard scale 3.5, and mixed step schedules to verify that negative conditioning is omitted and transformer batch sizing matches expectations. All 4 tests in the SD3 denoise test suite passed, and Ruff linter and formatter checks succeeded with zero issues.

label: Handle vanished worker sockets gracefully
diagramTitle: Treat vanished worker connections as cold sessions
footNote: Vanished sockets mean the worker stopped, which is a normal cold state rather than a system failure
title: Prevented UI crash when reattaching to idle agent sessions
summary: I fixed Ekko Studio's agent bridge so resuming an idle session whose worker socket has vanished is treated as an unloaded session instead of raising an error in the UI.
cvLine: Handled missing and disconnected worker IPC sockets during session status checks in Ekko Studio, preventing false failure errors when resuming idle agents; validated with 5 unit tests and full Vitest suite

story.title: Handle unloaded worker socket errors when resuming idle sessions
story.lead: When an agent worker process stopped or its socket file disappeared during idle cleanup, resuming the session triggered an unhandled socket error instead of marking the session as cold.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: In Ekko Studio's Hermes bridge broker, checking status for an existing session queried the worker process socket directly. If the worker was garbage-collected or its Unix domain socket disappeared right after the running check, the connection attempt threw a FileNotFoundError or ConnectionRefusedError. Because only RuntimeError was handled, the unhandled socket error bubbled up and caused session reattachment to fail with an error banner in the interface.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I updated BridgeBroker._status_if_loaded to query workers with start_if_needed=False so idle workers are not inadvertently respawned during status checks, and added error handling for OSError to treat vanished or refused sockets as cold, unloaded sessions. I also updated the facade WorkerProcess.request method to forward the start_if_needed parameter.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added a dedicated Python test fixture and Vitest test suite verifying that missing socket files, connection refusals, and skipped worker requests cleanly return unloaded session statuses while preserving standard runtime errors. All 5 test cases in the fixture passed, the Vitest integration suite passed, and project harness checks passed cleanly.

label: Send requests to the right AI service address
diagramTitle: Avoid adding a second version to the address
footNote: A versioned service address now reaches the intended endpoint
title: Fixed broken requests to versioned AI services
summary: I fixed Headroom’s proxy so requests reach AI services whose addresses already include a version, instead of returning a missing-page error.
cvLine: Corrected OpenAI-compatible proxy URL routing for versioned upstream bases, eliminating duplicated path segments and 404 responses; validated with 223 focused tests and 177 pre-push Python tests

story.title: Send AI requests to a versioned service address
story.lead: Some AI services include a version in their address. Headroom was adding another version when forwarding requests, which sent them to a path the service did not recognize.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: An AI service configured with an address ending in a version such as /v4 received requests with an extra /v1 in the path. In a real local HTTP check, that doubled path returned 404.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I changed how the proxy joins addresses: when the configured address ends in a numeric version, it removes only the incoming /v1 prefix. I added routing cases for versioned and unversioned addresses and kept the existing Copilot routes.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: The same local HTTP check reached the intended path and returned 200 after the fix. All 223 focused tests passed; the pre-push gate passed with 177 Python tests, 8 skips, Rust checks, and commitlint.

title: Prevent a connection error in Bedrock image requests
summary: I moved secure connection setup earlier so Bedrock image requests avoid a connection error caused by loading supporting libraries first.
cvLine: Initialized platform TLS trust before Hermes agent imports to prevent botocore SSL recursion in Bedrock image requests; validated with 1,223 passing tests and an offline real-library probe

story.title: Prepare secure connections before loading image services
story.lead: Bedrock image requests could fail when supporting libraries loaded before the bridge set up its trusted connections.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: A supporting library could keep an old secure connection class. Updating that class afterward caused repeated calls to itself when Bedrock tried to create a connection.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I moved the trust setup to immediately after bridge startup and before agent modules load. Older runtimes without the setup function still work.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: The full test suite passed 1,223 tests. An offline probe reproduced the recursion before the fix and created certificate-checking connections afterward. A live Bedrock request was not tested.

title: Made image annotations visible on transparent images

cvLine: Corrected OpenCV color handling for four-channel images so annotations retain visible alpha; validated with 7,559 fallback tests, 8,218 OpenCV tests and passing pre-commit hooks

story.title: Keep drawn labels visible on transparent images
story.lead: Supervision adds boxes, labels and other annotations to images. On transparent images, some of those marks disappeared.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: Drawing tools supplied three color values to images with four channels. The drawing library filled the missing transparency value with zero, making the marks invisible.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I made the shared drawing helper provide an opaque transparency value for four-channel images and used it across the affected drawing tools and annotators. Opacity settings still scale that value.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: Regression tests show the new marks are visible on transparent images and fail on the old code. The full suite passed with 7,559 tests on the fallback renderer and 8,218 with OpenCV; pre-commit hooks passed.

label: Allow proxy network ranges for public tools
diagramTitle: Accept public tool servers behind Fake-IP proxies
footNote: Public servers pass validation while internal addresses stay blocked
title: Allowed public tool servers to connect through local proxies
summary: I added an option to DeepTutor's tool validator so public MCP servers are not blocked when local DNS proxies return synthetic network addresses.
cvLine: Added configurable Fake-IP proxy range support to DeepTutor's strict MCP server URL validator, preventing false SSRF rejections for public tools behind local proxies while maintaining loopback and metadata guards; validated with 10 new regression tests (192 passing across the suite)

story.title: Let public tool servers connect when using local proxies
story.lead: DeepTutor checks addresses for tool servers to make sure they are on the public internet. Local proxies on macOS can make public servers look like private ones.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: When running with a local proxy in Fake-IP mode (such as Loon or Clash), DNS requests for public tool services return synthetic private addresses. DeepTutor's strict security check saw these private addresses and rejected public tool servers like GitMCP as forbidden private-network targets.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I introduced an opt-in environment setting that lets operators declare trusted proxy network ranges. When a hostname resolves within those ranges, the validator allows it as public, while IP-literal addresses, loopback routes, and cloud metadata targets remain strictly blocked.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added 10 unit tests covering IPv4 and IPv6 proxy ranges, IP literals, mixed DNS responses, and blocked metadata addresses. All 192 tests in the MCP test suite passed, and Ruff linting and formatting checks completed with zero errors.

label: Enforce 3D coordinates for plane geometry
title: Enforced 3D coordinate checks in plane geometry operations
summary: I fixed Kornia's 3D hyperplane methods to verify points have three coordinates, preventing single numbers from broadcasting into invalid 3D coordinates.
cvLine: Added 3D coordinate shape validation to hyperplane geometry methods to prevent invalid broadcasting; validated across 220 unit tests and 2,309 compile and ONNX conformance tests

story.title: Enforce 3D coordinate validation in plane geometry
story.lead: In Kornia's geometry module, 3D plane distance calculations accepted single-coordinate tensors and broadcast them into 3D points instead of rejecting them.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: When calculating distances or projections against a 3D hyperplane, passing a single-coordinate tensor broadcast against the 3D normal vector, returning distance calculations for an unintended point rather than raising a shape error.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I added shape validation in the signed distance method to ensure tensor points end in exactly three coordinates before performing vector math, which automatically protects distance and projection operations.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: The fix was verified with 220 passing plane geometry tests, including a new regression test covering 24 invalid-shape cases, along with 764 compile conformance tests and 1,545 ONNX conformance tests.

title: Stopped secret API key echoing and credential requests in chat
summary: I fixed OpenMontage's image generation skill and docs to verify API keys without printing them to output and stopped agents from asking users for secrets in chat.
cvLine: Patched image-generation agent skill instructions to prevent secret API key echoing and direct users to configuration files rather than requesting raw credentials in chat; validated with 242 contract and integrity tests

story.title: Prevent secret key exposure in agent image generation
story.lead: In OpenMontage's BFL FLUX image generation skill, setup instructions echoed secret API keys into terminal output and prompted agents to ask users for credentials in chat.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: The setup instructions for the BFL image generation skill used echo $BFL_API_KEY to check if a key was set, which printed the raw API key to standard output. Additionally, the reference docs directed agents to ask users to paste their secret API keys directly into chat when missing.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I replaced the echo commands with safe non-printing presence checks across the skill and reference documentation. I also updated the setup workflow to instruct users to configure their environment file directly instead of sharing secrets in chat, and added an automated contract test to enforce these rules.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I verified the changes by running the contract test suite, where all 242 tests passed, confirming that no skill files echo the secret key or prompt users to paste credentials in chat.
